what: Importing Data from a CSV File
title: Visualise Sports Injuries With Anatomical Heatmaps
text: injury data lives CSV file, package provides helpers full workflow: create template, fill , read back, plot. 1. Create template CSV 18 recognised body subcategories one empty column per sport: 2. Fill file favourite spreadsheet editor, entering injury frequencies region_area grouping row. 3. Read file back . read_injury_data() checks required columns present, least one sport column exists, sport values numeric (warning values fail parse): 4. Plot usual:
code: create_injury_template("injuries.csv", sports = c("boxing", "judo")) df <- read_injury_data("injuries.csv") injury_heatmap(df, "boxing", "front", sex = "male")

title: Visualise Sports Injuries With Anatomical Heatmaps
text: Start creating data frame: run injury_heatmap(injury_data, selected_sport, view_choice) : injury_data: data used, .e. data frame selected_sport: column name use view_choice: view diagram. One : "front", "back", "" Run ?injury_heatmap detail.
code: subcategory <- c("Head","Neck","Shoulder","Chest","Upper Arm","Elbow",                  "Abdomen","Forearm","Hip Groin","Wrist","Hand",                  "Thigh","Knee","Lower Leg","Ankle","Foot","Thoracic Spine","Lumbosacral")  region_area <- rep("Example", length(subcategory)) boxing <- c(15, 5, 18, 12, 20, 6, 10, 14, 9, 9, 11, 3, 16, 13, 7, 8, 18, 22)  df <- data.frame(region_area, subcategory, boxing) injury_heatmap(df, "boxing", "front", sex = "male", show_scale = FALSE)

title: spinviz 0.0.1.0000
text: required column names injury data standardised snake_case: Region.area now region_area Subcategory now subcategory. affects create_injury_template(), read_injury_data(), injury_heatmap(). Existing CSV files using old names must updated; read_injury_data() now errors old names hint explaining rename. Example sport columns README template now use lowercase names (e.g. sport1 instead Sport_1) consistency. Sport column names remain free-form.

title: spinviz 0.0.1.0000
text: New create_injury_template() writes template CSV pre-filled recognised body subcategories one column per requested sport, ready filled injury frequencies. New read_injury_data() reads validates CSV, checking required region_area/subcategory columns, least one sport column, unrecognised (possibly misspelled) subcategory values. Files read check.names = FALSE user-supplied column names preserved exactly written. Added rsvg Imports. required runtime magick::image_read_svg() rendering SVG body diagrams, absence caused failures systems (e.g. CI runners) already installed. Removed duplicate grDevices entry DESCRIPTION Imports. Added tests/testthat suite covering diagram_colours(), test_colour(), injury_heatmap(). injury_heatmap() longer calls print() result returning , previously caused plot render twice R Markdown/Quarto documents call left unassigned. injury_heatmap() now warns values selected sport column converted numeric, instead silently coercing NA. injury_heatmap()’s documentation palette argument now regenerated longer shows stale “WIP” placeholder text. injury_heatmap()’s front/back label coordinate tables now built single shared lookup (label_position_lookup()) instead two hand-duplicated tables, views silently drift apart. injury_heatmap()’s combined “views” label table (both_label_position_lookup()) now validates front-/back-regions single source truth (view_exclusive_regions()) used SVG id per-view label lookups, instead re-encoding regions one-sided third time. test_colour() now restores caller’s graphics::par() settings exit instead permanently changing plotting layout (mfrow). Fixed documentation typo test_colour() (“coloublind” -> “colourblind”).
